title: Librarian has evidence authority, not decision authority
summary: Librarian distinguishes sources, occurrences, propositions and events. It reconstructs who communicated a claim, when, and what evidence was available; it must not promote lexical scores, sentiment, bias labels, corrections or source metadata into truth, editorial intent, action authorisation or causal authority. A retraction withdraws an assertion but does not prove that the proposition is false.
invariants: Keep event, proposition, text occurrence, communicative intention, source authority and downstream decision separate.
Assess bias as evidence-bound comparative framing, selection, omission and context: absence of observations is not evidence of omission without sampling completeness.
Respect privacy and the sampled cohort: comparable source populations require explicit frame, date, audience, geography and collection completeness.
Outputs are observations, citations and uncertainty; CMS, Brand Effect and Reputation Effect retain their own governed decisions.

provenance.claim: Experimental evidence objects rather than legacy inheritance.
